resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1962 item says the Forest Service built the building in 1916; a 1913 item already names a Castle Peak Lookout station. Both are recorded and the story does not choose between them.

The register lists the Bureau of Land Management as administrator of the site; the 1962 item and the westlookouts header describe a Forest Service lookout (Holy Cross, then White River National Forest). Both are recorded.
The 1962 item says the building would soon come down; the register says it was removed in the late 1960s with no exact year. The story gives the register's dating.

sources.title: Castle Peak - Forest Lookouts (newspaper items transcribed)

notes_for_editor: Newspaper items are read from a lookout-history site's transcriptions, not scanned originals. Elevation differs by source: 10,974 ft for the register's site, 11,434 ft in the 1919 guidebook, and about 11,305 ft for the peak on Wikipedia (not used in the story). Staffing rests only on 1919-1921 newspaper items. The brief's agency field (BLM) is supported by the register and left unchanged. Nominator name from the register is kept in the 2011 event note.
